key_insight: EEG-Xplain provides a unified, multimodal attribution framework to make black-box EEG foundation models interpretable across spatial, temporal, and frequency dimensions.
engineering_relevance: It enables more trustworthy deployment of EEG models in clinical and neuroengineering settings by standardizing explanation, reliability testing, and report generation.
method: Combines gradient-, perturbation-, and activation-based attribution methods across heterogeneous EEG architectures.
Maps important EEG channels and time segments with topographic and heatmap visualizations.
Uses spectral perturbation plus AOPC and cross-method consistency to evaluate explanation reliability, then converts results into LLM-generated natural-language reports.
evidence_signal: Experiments on Mumtaz2016 and TUAB show the explanations align with known neurophysiological markers while also revealing artifacts and spurious dependencies.
watch_item: Attribution results may still be sensitive to noise, artifacts, and method choice, so explanation consistency does not guarantee true causal understanding.
paper_title: EEG-Xplain: Decoding Neural Black-Boxes of EEG Foundation Models
